report.source_text: The biopsy revealed a basaloid cutaneous lesion consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma, as observed in the H&E histological section (figure 1). Immunohistochemistry was performed, revealing that the lesion exhibited patchy infiltrates positively staining for epithelial membrane antigen, specifically staining the apical aspect of the pseudo glandular cyst (figure 2A). Additionally, there was diffuse positive staining for pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3) (figure 2B).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 20s presented with a 4-month history of persistent, progressively enlarging, and intermittently uncomfortable swelling with pruritus on her right posterior scalp. Dermatological examination revealed two lesions. Sonographic evaluation showed two adjacent hypoechoic lesions in the parietal region, resembling epidermoid cysts. An initial biopsy revealed a basaloid cutaneous lesion consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma, with immunohistochemistry showing positive staining for epithelial membrane antigen and pan-cytokeratin. The final diagnosis states that histopathological examination of excised tissue confirmed PCACC, but the specific report for this excised tissue was not provided.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with persistent swelling and pruritus on the right posterior scalp with two lesions: a 12 mm subcutaneous cystic lesion and an 11 mm erythematous lesion.
Sonographic evaluation revealed two adjacent hypoechoic lesions in the parietal region, resembling epidermoid cysts (largest 10x8 mm).
Biopsy revealed a basaloid cutaneous lesion consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma, with positive staining for epithelial membrane antigen and pan-cytokeratin.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial sonographic evaluation suggested epidermoid cysts, but subsequent biopsy findings of adenoid cystic carcinoma superseded this.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific histopathological report of the excised tissue that definitively confirmed the diagnosis of PCACC.
